cards.text: Balak, king of Moab, brought Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel, and twice it came out a blessing. So Balak takes him to a THIRD hilltop, the top of Peor, like a man walking around the house hunting for one more bar of signal. Up there, Balaam sees that it pleases the LORD to bless Israel.

cards.question: This third time, Balaam goes off to seek omens like he did before.
Instead of seeking omens, Balaam turns his face toward the ___.

cards.text: Balaam looks up and sees Israel camped tribe by tribe. And then something comes upon him.

cards.question: As Balaam looks out at Israel's camp, the ___ of God comes upon him.

cards.text: Balaam lifts up an oracle and opens with a big introduction: Balaam son of Beor, a man whose eyes are open, who hears the words of God and sees a vision from the Almighty. Friend, I've got a mustache for hands and a gold base for feet, and even I don't introduce myself like THAT.
Then he looks out over the camp and says, “How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!” Balak paid this man to curse those tents, and he's out here complimenting the decor.

cards.question: Balaam keeps describing Israel's camp spread out below him. What kind of picture does he paint?

answers.text: Gardens and trees growing by water
Walls and towers built for battle
Dust and ruins left after a storm

cards.text: Water will flow from his buckets, Balaam says. Then he talks about Israel's king and brings up Agag, a name the Bible later gives a king of the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15:8).

cards.question: Balaam says Israel's king will be greater than Agag.

cards.text: Balaam says God brought Israel out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox. Then he pictures Israel lying down like a lion and asks, “who dares to rouse him?”

cards.question: Balaam ends this oracle with a line about anyone who curses Israel. What does he say happens to them?

answers.text: They are spared in the end

cards.text: Balak's anger burns against Balaam, and he strikes his hands together. That's the clap of a man opening a bill he did NOT see coming.

cards.question: Balak tells Balaam he has blessed his enemies ___ times now.
Balak has had enough of Balaam's blessings. What does he tell Balaam to do?

answers.text: Flee at once to his home
Try again from a fourth hilltop

cards.question: Balak says it's the LORD who has kept Balaam from his reward.

cards.text: Balaam answers Balak by pointing back to what he already told the messengers Balak sent him. Friend, this is a “per my last email” moment.

cards.question: Balaam says even Balak's house full of silver and gold couldn't get him to do one thing. What is it?

answers.text: Go beyond the command of the LORD
Leave his own people behind for good
Bless the people of Moab instead

cards.question: Balaam says he's going back to his people. But before he leaves, what does he offer Balak?

answers.text: A warning about what Israel will do to Moab
A promise to come back and try once more
A blessing on Moab for the days ahead

cards.text: So Balaam lifts up another oracle with the same kind of introduction, plus one new line: he has knowledge from the Most High. Hey, I KNOW that name, that's the One who sent an angel to my junk drawer.
Then Balaam says something that makes me lean in: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near.”

cards.question: Balaam says, “I see him, but not now.” What does that tell you about the one he's seeing?

answers.text: He's in Israel's camp right now

cards.text: Balaam goes on, “A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel.” A STAR, friend, my boy Berry would have his face pressed to the window for this one.

cards.question: A star from Jacob and a scepter from Israel. What is Balaam picturing?

answers.text: A king rising up from Israel
A temple rising up in Israel
A harvest rising up in Israel

cards.question: Balaam is warning Balak, king of Moab. He says this coming one will crush the skulls of ___.

cards.text: He'll strike down all the sons of Sheth too, and Balak is standing right there for it. That's hiring a guy to trash the bakery across the street, and he comes back saying that bakery's gonna buy YOURS.

cards.question: Next Balaam talks about Edom, the nation that came from Esau (Genesis 36:1). He says Edom will become a possession.

cards.text: Balaam says, “A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city.” Then he sees Amalek, the nation that attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8).

cards.question: Balaam says Amalek was first among the nations. What does he say Amalek's end will be?

cards.text: Next he sees the Kenites, the people of Moses' father-in-law (Judges 1:16). Balaam tells them, “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.”

cards.question: Balaam says the Kenites' cliff home will keep them safe forever.
Who does Balaam say will take the Kenites captive?

cards.text: Once more Balaam lifts up an oracle: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?”

cards.question: Ships come from the coasts of Cyprus and subdue Asshur and Eber, but Balaam says they too will ___ forever.
After all the oracles, Balaam goes back to his homeland and Balak goes on his way.

cards.text: Balaam heads home, Balak goes his way, and the man never got his curse. He tried hill after hill, friend, and God's answer came out the same from every single one.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "I see him, but not now.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card tells facts from Numbers 22: Balak is king of Moab (22:4) and he brought Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel (22:5-6). But it cites only Numbers 23:11-24:1, so the citation is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says Balaam blessed Israel twice and that Balak took him to a THIRD hilltop. That gives away the answer "three" before the baker gets to this fill in the blank.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Balak strikes his hands together in anger. The comparison is someone opening a bill they didn't expect, and people don't clap when they open a bill. The everyday image doesn't share the core action, so the joke doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This last story card retells Numbers 24:25, which card 16 just asked about (Balaam goes home and Balak goes his way). It then sums up the whole episode. It adds nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap card.
